Muckraking wasn't limited to newspapers and magazines. Many journalists also wrote books during the Progressive Era to expose problems. Upton Sinclair's novel
(1906) told the story of a Lithuanian immigrant's experience working in a Chicago meatpacking factory. It included shocking descriptions of meatpacking factory conditions.

contents.text: Sinclair wanted to demonstrate how terribly workers were treated, but readers were more shocked by the disgusting ways food was handled. The public was furious, so Congress had to act. In 1906, it passed the Meat Inspection Act and the Pure Food and Drug Act. These new laws made sure food was safe to eat.

contents.text: Major events also caused changes during the Progressive Era. Read the passage about one such event. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: In 1909, workers at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory, a New York clothing manufacturer, demanded higher pay and safer working conditions. The factory owners rejected workers' demands, claiming they would be too costly.

Just over a year later, on March 25, 1911, a fire broke out at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory. As flames spread through the building, workers—mostly young immigrant women—ran to escape but found the exit doors locked. Hundreds of people were trapped inside overcrowded rooms filled with fabric that quickly caught on fire.

In total, 146 workers died in the fire. The factory's owners were arrested but were found not guilty after a brief trial. The lack of justice for the victims sparked public outrage and increased pressure on politicians to enforce safety regulations on businesses.

contents.text: Major events also caused changes during the Progressive Era. Read the passage about one such event. Then follow the directions below.

textContent.text: In 1909, workers at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory, a New York clothing manufacturer, demanded higher pay and safer working conditions. The factory owners rejected workers' demands, claiming they would be too costly.

Just over a year later, on March 25, 1911, a fire broke out at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory. As flames spread through the building, workers—mostly young immigrant women—ran to escape but found the exit doors locked. Hundreds of people were trapped inside overcrowded rooms filled with fabric that quickly caught on fire.

In total, 146 workers died in the fire. The factory's owners were arrested but were found not guilty after a brief trial. The lack of justice for the victims sparked public outrage and increased pressure on politicians to enforce safety regulations on businesses.

textContent.text: In 1909, workers at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory, a New York clothing manufacturer, demanded higher pay and safer working conditions. The factory owners rejected workers' demands, claiming they would be too costly.

contents.text: Major events also caused changes during the Progressive Era. Read the passage about one such event. Then follow the directions below.

textContent.text: In 1909, workers at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory, a New York clothing manufacturer, demanded higher pay and safer working conditions. The factory owners rejected workers' demands, claiming they would be too costly.

Just over a year later, on March 25, 1911, a fire broke out at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory. As flames spread through the building, workers—mostly young immigrant women—ran to escape but found the exit doors locked. Hundreds of people were trapped inside overcrowded rooms filled with fabric that quickly caught on fire.

In total, 146 workers died in the fire. The factory's owners were arrested but were found not guilty after a brief trial. The lack of justice for the victims sparked public outrage and increased pressure on politicians to enforce safety regulations on businesses.
